name: sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export
prose: Precondition: argp points to a kernel copy of a sev_issue_cmd whose data field is a user pointer to a sev_user_data_pdh_cert_export that must be readable and also writable (the function writes it back); writable says whether the file was opened for writing; the caller holds the SEV command lock needed by __sev_do_cmd_locked. Behaviour: it returns -EFAULT if copy_from_user of the input struct fails. If any of the four user addresses or lengths in the input is zero it treats the call as a length query and skips the allocations; otherwise it returns -EFAULT if either requested length exceeds SEV_FW_BLOB_MAX_SIZE, returns -ENOMEM if the first kzalloc fails, and returns -ENOMEM after freeing the first blob if the second fails. If the platform is not in SEV_STATE_INIT it returns -EPERM when writable is false, or tries sev_move_to_init_state and returns its error (the blobs freed) on failure. It then calls __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_PDH_CERT_EXPORT) and always copies the firmware-reported lengths back into the user input struct; if that copy_to_user fails the result is -EFAULT (overriding the command result). Otherwise, if the command returned an error it returns that error, and if the command returned 0 but argp->error is nonzero it warns once and returns 0, in both cases without copying the blob contents. Otherwise it copies the PDH blob and then the cert chain blob to the user addresses, returning -EFAULT if a copy fails. On every path after the INIT-state check it shuts the firmware down with __sev_firmware_shutdown if sev_move_to_init_state requested it, and frees both blobs; the early -EFAULT returns happen before anything was allocated.
note: checked sev-dev.c:2250-2351 (slice cut head). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (copy_to_user(argp->data,&input) at line 2321); round 2 claim consistent with code (returns the __sev_do_cmd_locked error); original claim RIGHT (0 with argp->error set).

name: snp_map_cmd_buf_desc
prose: Precondition: desc points to a cmd_buf_desc with paddr_ptr, len and guest_owned set; if len is nonzero *desc->paddr_ptr is the physical address of the command buffer. Behaviour: if desc->len is 0 it returns 0 and changes nothing. If the descriptor is not guest owned it allocates a bounce buffer with alloc_pages of order get_order(len) (2^order pages, not get_order(len) pages), returning -ENOMEM with nothing changed if that fails; otherwise it saves the original *paddr_ptr in desc->paddr_orig and overwrites *paddr_ptr with the bounce buffer's physical address (no data is copied by this function); for a guest-owned descriptor neither is done. It then calls rmp_mark_pages_firmware(*paddr_ptr, PAGE_ALIGN(len) >> PAGE_SHIFT, true) and returns 0 on success. If that call fails it prints a warning and returns -EFAULT without freeing the bounce buffer and without restoring *paddr_ptr or paddr_orig.
note: checked sev-dev.c:684-714. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (order semantics and no rollback on failure); round 2 RIGHT (paddr_orig only set for non-guest-owned). The old claim that the pages are 'not firmware-owned' after failure was removed: the state left by a failed rmp_mark_pages_firmware is not visible here.

name: sfs_dev_init
prose: Precondition: psp is a valid psp_device with a device psp->dev. Behaviour: it allocates the sfs_device with devm_kzalloc (returning -ENOMEM if that fails) and a 2MB command buffer with snp_alloc_hv_fixed_pages; if that fails it goes to cleanup_dev, returning the initial value -ENOMEM. It marks the buffer uncacheable with set_memory_uc; on failure it frees the HV-fixed pages (without calling set_memory_wb) and cleans up, returning that error. It then sets psp->sfs_data and the dev/psp back-pointers and calls sfs_misc_init; if that fails it restores write-back caching with set_memory_wb, frees the HV-fixed pages and cleans up, returning that error. On success it logs a notice and returns 0 leaving psp->sfs_data set. The cleanup_dev label sets psp->sfs_data to NULL and frees the devm allocation with devm_kfree on all failure paths.
note: slice cut head; real function is sfs_dev_init (sfs.c:251-311), sfs_init does not exist. Old prose said the value of ret on page-allocation failure was 'not set by this path': it is the initial -ENOMEM.

name: sp_pci_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is the PCI device being probed and id->driver_data should point to an sp_dev_vdata. Behaviour: it allocates the sp_device (sp_alloc_struct) and a devm sp_pci, returning -ENOMEM through the e_err label if either fails; it returns -ENODEV (error printed) if id->driver_data is NULL; it calls pcim_enable_device, pci_select_bars and pcim_iomap_regions and returns their errors; it returns -ENOMEM if pcim_iomap_table returns NULL or the BAR chosen by sp->dev_vdata->bar is not mapped; and it calls sp_get_irqs, returning its error via e_err (without sp_free_irqs). After that it sets bus mastering and the PSP master-device callbacks, sets the DMA mask to 48 bits and, if that fails, to 32 bits, going to free_irqs with that error if the 32-bit mask also fails. It stores sp as the device's drvdata and calls sp_init; if that fails it goes to free_irqs with its error. On success it returns 0. free_irqs calls sp_free_irqs and then e_err prints a notice and returns the error; the drvdata is therefore set at the time of an sp_init failure but not for the earlier failures, and the PCI device enable and BAR mappings are released by devres.
note: slice cut head; function is sp-pci.c:231-316. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: sp_get_irqs failure jumps to e_err (line 284-286), so sp_free_irqs is only called for the DMA-mask failure and the sp_init failure.

name: cc_aead_alloc
prose: Precondition: drvdata is the CryptoCell driver data with hw_rev and std_bodies set. Behaviour: this is the whole function cc_aead_alloc; the slice shows its algorithm loop and unwind. It allocates the AEAD handle with devm_kmalloc (-ENOMEM if that fails), initialises its list, stores it in drvdata->aead_handle and allocates MAX_HMAC_DIGEST_SIZE bytes of SRAM workspace with cc_sram_alloc (-ENOMEM via fail1 if it returns NULL_SRAM_ADDR). For each entry of aead_algs it skips (continue) entries whose min_hw_rev exceeds drvdata->hw_rev or whose std_body is not in drvdata->std_bodies, otherwise it creates the algorithm with cc_create_aead_alg (jumping to fail1 with the error from PTR_ERR on failure), registers it with crypto_register_aead (jumping to fail1 with that error on failure, the failed algorithm not being added to the list) and adds it to the handle's list. It returns 0 after the loop. The fail1 label calls cc_aead_free, which unregisters and removes the algorithms already on the list, and then returns the error. The function does not copy tfm or context fields and does not allocate key buffers; those are done elsewhere (cc_aead_init).
note: slice cut head; real function is cc_aead_alloc (cc_aead.c:2611-2668), no cc_aead_init in this slice (cc_aead_init is at line 125 and is a different function). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the code allocates SRAM and registers algorithms; the old prose described a different function.

name: safexcel_send_req
prose: Precondition: base, sreq, src, dst, cryptlen, assoclen, digestsize, iv, commands and results describe a prepared request for ring ring, and ctx->key/ctx->key_len hold the key. Behaviour: the function is safexcel_send_req (the slice begins mid-body). It counts the source entries needed for cryptlen + assoclen, for AEAD adjusts the destination length by the digest size (minus for decrypt, plus otherwise) and copies the ipad/opad state into the context record, and for CBC decrypt first saves the last IV block of the source into areq->iv (these writes happen before any mapping and stay on failure). It returns -EINVAL if the in-place buffer is too small (nr_src <= 0 while a length is nonzero) or if, for src != dst, the source or destination list is too small, and returns -EIO if dma_map_sg of the source fails; if the destination length check or the destination dma_map_sg fails after the source was mapped, it jumps to the unmap label, which unmaps src and, when nr_dst > 0, dst. It then copies the key into the context record, adds command descriptors (a dummy one if the input length is zero, otherwise one per source segment up to the request length), writes the context control and token, and adds result descriptors for the destination (skipping AAD, or a dummy one for the AEAD decrypt with only AAD), returning the PTR_ERR of any failed descriptor allocation after rolling back the result and command ring write pointers added so far and unmapping src (and dst when src != dst). On success it queues the request with safexcel_rdr_req_set, stores the descriptor counts in *commands and *results, and returns 0, leaving the DMA mappings to be released at completion. *commands and *results are not modified on failure.
note: slice cut head; real name is safexcel_send_req (safexcel_cipher.c:673-916). Checked every return. Old prose omitted the source-buffer -EINVAL, the pre-mapping side effects, and that the destination unmap at the unmap label also runs after the destination's own mapping failure.

name: iaa_crypto_debugfs_init
prose: Precondition: none; an __init function. Behaviour: it returns -ENODEV without creating anything if debugfs_initialized() is false. Otherwise it creates the "iaa_crypto" debugfs directory, storing it in iaa_crypto_debugfs_root, then creates the global_stats, wq_stats and stats_reset files (mode 0644) under it, ignoring the return values of the create calls, and returns 0.
note: iaa_crypto_stats.c:258-273. Contract left empty because the return is an errno and it writes global state.

name: kmb_ocs_hcu_do_one_request
prose: Precondition: areq is the ahash request queued on the crypto engine, with its request and transform contexts set up. Behaviour: it finds the HCU device with kmb_ocs_hcu_find_dev and goes to the error label with -ENOENT if there is none. If REQ_FLAGS_HMAC_HW is set it maps the data (kmb_ocs_dma_prepare), runs ocs_hcu_hmac, cleans up the DMA list in any case, and goes to done on success or error on failure, skipping the final buffer wipe. If REQ_FINAL is clear it returns -EINVAL immediately, without wiping the buffer or finalizing the request, when there is no input data; otherwise it maps the data, calls ocs_hcu_hash_update, cleans up the DMA list, then resets buf_cnt and copies the leftover scatterlist data into the request buffer with flush_sg_to_ocs_buffer and goes to done, or to error if any step fails. For a final request it uses ocs_hcu_hash_finup (with DMA mapping and cleanup) when there is data, otherwise ocs_hcu_hash_final, and, for REQ_FLAGS_HMAC_SW, builds the key-xor-opad block plus the digest in the request buffer and hashes it with ocs_hcu_digest; any failing step goes to the error label. After a final request it wipes the request buffer (kmb_ocs_hcu_secure_cleanup) and falls into done. The done label calls crypto_finalize_hash_request with status 0 and returns 0; the error label only wipes the buffer with kmb_ocs_hcu_secure_cleanup and returns the error, so the request is not finalized with an error status.
note: checked keembay-ocs-hcu-core.c:420-568. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: the error path (565-567) does not call crypto_finalize_hash_request; round 2 RIGHT (final finup/final path and non-update flows); original RIGHT (-EINVAL returned directly). The old prose said the buffer is zeroed on every success; update and HW-HMAC successes skip the wipe (they go to done).

name: adf_set_hb_counters_fail
prose: Precondition: accel_dev->heartbeat->dma.virt_addr points to a table of hb_cnt_pair entries holding at least 2 * max_aes * hb_ctrs entries (max_aes from hw_device->get_num_aes, hb_ctrs from hw_device->num_hb_ctrs), and ae * hb_ctrs + thr is below max_aes * hb_ctrs. Behaviour: it reads the u16 resp_heartbeat_cnt of the pair at index thr_id = ae * hb_ctrs + thr in the first block, increments that pair's req_heartbeat_cnt by one, and then stores the value it read into resp_heartbeat_cnt of the pair at the same index in the second block (offset by max_aes * hb_ctrs entries). It changes no other entry and returns nothing. The comment in the code says it injects live.req != live.rsp, but the code does not guarantee that for arbitrary starting counter values.
note: adf_heartbeat_inject.c:23-40. Reviewer rounds 1, 2 and 15 RIGHT: the second block is written, and live.req != live.rsp is not guaranteed (the old closing claim was dropped).

name: qat_rsa_enc
prose: Precondition: req is an akcipher request on a qat_rsa_ctx. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if ctx->n or ctx->e is NULL; returns -EOVERFLOW after setting req->dst_len to ctx->key_sz if req->dst_len < ctx->key_sz; returns -EINVAL if req->src_len > ctx->key_sz or if no PKE function id exists for the key size. It fills the request message, then (error value -ENOMEM) maps the source: directly if it is a single scatterlist entry of exactly key_sz bytes, otherwise through a kzalloc'd copy src_align (returning -ENOMEM if that fails); a dma_map_single error goes to the unwind code with -ENOMEM. It does the same for the destination (dst_align) and then maps the input and output parameter blocks; any mapping or allocation failure unwinds the mappings made so far and frees src_align and dst_align with kfree_sensitive and returns -ENOMEM. It then returns the value of qat_alg_send_asym_message; only if that value is -ENOSPC does it unmap everything and free the buffers before returning it; for 0 or any other value the mappings and buffers stay for the completion callback.
note: slice cut head; function is qat_asym_algs.c:698-830. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the DMA-mapping failure paths return -ENOMEM after cleanup (lines 765-766, 780-781, 788-795).

name: otx2_sg_info_create
prose: Precondition: pdev and req are valid; req->in and req->out describe in_cnt and out_cnt gather/scatter entries. Behaviour: it returns NULL (after logging) if in_cnt or out_cnt exceeds OTX2_CPT_MAX_SG_IN_CNT or OTX2_CPT_MAX_SG_OUT_CNT, and NULL if the kzalloc of the info buffer fails. It computes the gather and scatter list lengths, sets info->dlen, in_buffer and out_buffer, writes the 8-byte SG list header, and sets up the gather and scatter components with setup_sgio_components; if either fails it calls otx2_cpt_info_destroy and returns NULL. It sets dma_len and maps in_buffer with dma_map_single (DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL); a mapping error also calls otx2_cpt_info_destroy and returns NULL. On success it sets completion_addr and comp_baddr past the SG lists and returns the info, which holds the DMA mapping to be released with otx2_cpt_info_destroy.
note: slice cut head; real name is otx2_sg_info_create (otx2_cpt_reqmgr.h:449-561); no otx2_cpt_info_create. Old prose omitted the too-many-components and kzalloc NULL returns.

name: otx2_cpt_discover_eng_capabilities
prose: Precondition: cptpf is the CPT physical function with its engine groups and LF state set up. Behaviour: it returns 0 immediately, changing nothing, if cptpf->is_eng_caps_discovered is already true. Otherwise it creates the capability-discovery engine groups (create_eng_caps_discovery_grps) and initialises the LFs with otx2_cptlf_init; either failure jumps to delete_grps with that error (after LF init failure the LFs are not shut down). It then kzallocs a buffer (-ENOMEM, via lf_cleanup, if that fails), maps it with dma_map_single (-EFAULT if the mapping fails), builds a LOAD_FVC command, and for each engine type from 1 to OTX2_CPT_MAX_ENG_TYPES-1 sends it, polls for completion up to a timeout and stores the 64-bit big-endian result in cptpf->eng_caps[etype]; if the poll times out it logs a warning, sets is_eng_caps_discovered to false and returns -ENODEV (capabilities of earlier types having already been stored). If all types complete it sets is_eng_caps_discovered to true and returns 0. On both the success path and the post-mapping failure paths it unmaps and frees the buffer, shuts down the LFs and deletes the engine groups before returning, so that cleanup is not specific to failure.
note: slice cut head; real function is otx2_cpt_discover_eng_capabilities (otx2_cptpf_ucode.c:1489-1596). Old prose said cleanup on failure only; the labels are also reached on success (lines 1580-1596).

name: NX842_COUNTER_INC(comp_complete)
prose: Generated function nx842_inc_comp_complete(dev), a static inline expanded from NX842_COUNTER_INC(comp_complete). Precondition: dev may be NULL; if it is non-NULL, dev->counters must be a valid pointer. Behaviour: if dev is non-NULL it atomically increments dev->counters->comp_complete with atomic64_inc, and otherwise it does nothing; it returns nothing.
note: nx-common-pseries.c:139-145 macro definition and instantiation.

name: NX842DEV_COUNTER_ATTR_RO(comp_complete)
prose: Generated function nx842_comp_complete_show(dev, attr, buf), expanded from NX842DEV_COUNTER_ATTR_RO(comp_complete) through nx842_counter_read. Precondition: buf is a sysfs page of PAGE_SIZE bytes. Behaviour: it takes rcu_read_lock, reads the global devdata pointer with rcu_dereference, and if it is non-NULL writes the value of atomic64_read of the comp_complete counter as "%lld\n" into buf with snprintf limited to PAGE_SIZE, returning the snprintf result; if devdata is NULL it returns 0 and writes nothing to buf. It releases the RCU read lock before returning and keeps no reference; rcu_read_lock may be nested, so the caller may already hold the RCU read lock.
note: nx-common-pseries.c:878-901. Removed the old claim that the caller must not hold the RCU read lock (not required by rcu_read_lock).

name: ahash_setkey
prose: Precondition: tfm is a talitos ahash transform and the transform context's key buffer can hold a key of up to the block size or the digest size. Behaviour: this is the whole function ahash_setkey; the slice shows its tail. If keylen is no more than the block size it copies the key into ctx->key; otherwise it computes the digest of the key with keyhash and returns -EINVAL if that fails (ctx unchanged), or copies the digest into ctx->key and uses the digest size as the key size. It then unmaps the previous key mapping with dma_unmap_single if ctx->keylen was nonzero, sets ctx->keylen to the key size, maps ctx->key with dma_map_single into ctx->dma_key (the mapping result is not checked) and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is ahash_setkey (talitos.c:2297-2328). Fixed under the real name instead of dropping.

name: DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT(4ch, TALITOS2_ISR_4CHDONE, TALITOS2_ISR_4CHERR, 0)
prose: Generated function talitos2_interrupt_4ch(irq, data), expanded from DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT(4ch, TALITOS2_ISR_4CHDONE, TALITOS2_ISR_4CHERR, 0). Precondition: data is the struct device whose drvdata is the talitos_private, and the caller does not hold priv->reg_lock. Behaviour: it takes priv->reg_lock with interrupts saved, reads ISR and ISR_LO, acknowledges by writing ICR = isr & (4CHDONE | 4CHERR) and ICR_LO = isr_lo. If isr & 4CHERR or isr_lo is nonzero it releases the lock and calls talitos_error(dev, isr & 4CHERR, isr_lo); otherwise, if isr & 4CHDONE is nonzero, it clears the 4CHDONE bits in IMR and schedules priv->done_task[0], and then releases the lock. It returns IRQ_HANDLED if (isr & (4CHDONE | 4CHERR)) or isr_lo is nonzero, else IRQ_NONE.
note: talitos.c:787-820; matches the macro body (lines 788-817).

name: DEF_TALITOS2_INTERRUPT(ch0_2, TALITOS2_ISR_CH_0_2_DONE, TALITOS2_ISR_CH_0_2_ERR, 0)

Precondition: data is the struct device whose drvdata is the talitos_private, and the caller does not hold priv->reg_lock. If isr & CH_0_2_ERR or isr_lo is nonzero it releases the lock and calls talitos_error(dev, isr & CH_0_2_ERR, isr_lo); otherwise, if isr & CH_0_2_DONE is nonzero, it clears those bits in IMR and schedules priv->done_task[0], and then releases the lock. It returns IRQ_HANDLED if (isr & (CH_0_2_DONE | CH_0_2_ERR)) or isr_lo is nonzero, else IRQ_NONE.
note: talitos.c:821-822 instantiation of the macro at 787-817.

It returns IRQ_HANDLED if (isr & (CH_1_3_DONE | CH_1_3_ERR)) or isr_lo is nonzero, else IRQ_NONE.

name: virtcrypto_algo_is_supported
prose: Precondition: vcrypto is a virtio_crypto device with its service and algorithm masks set. Behaviour: it computes service_mask = 1u << service (no check that service is below 32, so a larger value is an undefined shift) and, if algo is greater than 31, subtracts 32 from algo and remembers that the high mask applies. It returns false if the service bit is clear in vcrypto->crypto_services. It then picks an algorithm mask by service: for CIPHER cipher_algo_l or cipher_algo_h, for MAC mac_algo_l or mac_algo_h, for HASH hash_algo, for AEAD aead_algo, for AKCIPHER akcipher_algo (HASH, AEAD and AKCIPHER use their single mask regardless of the high/low choice), and for any other service the mask stays 0. It returns false if bit (1u << algo) (with algo already reduced) is clear in that mask (a shift count of 32 or more is again undefined), and true otherwise. It takes no locks.
note: slice cut head; real name is virtcrypto_algo_is_supported (virtio_crypto_mgr.c:243-293). The old claim that it returns false for service > 31 is not in the code (no such check).

name: CXL_ECS_GET_ATTR(threshold)
prose: Generated function cxl_ecs_get_threshold(dev, drv_data, fru_id, val), expanded from CXL_ECS_GET_ATTR(threshold). Precondition: drv_data is an initialised cxl_ecs_context and fru_id indexes one of its media FRUs (the index is not range-checked). Behaviour: it calls cxl_mem_ecs_get_attrbs, which allocates a buffer and reads the current ECS attributes; if that fails it returns its error (-ENOMEM or -EIO) with *val unmodified. Otherwise it stores in *val the value cxl_get_ecs_threshold computes as ecs_supp_threshold[config & 0x7] and returns 0. The table has entries only for indices 3, 4 and 5 (256, 1024, 4096), so indices 0, 1 and 2 give 0, and indices 6 and 7 read past the end of the 6-entry table.
note: checked edac.c:512-535, 541-574, 634-665. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: indices 6 and 7 are out of bounds, not 0; indices 0-2 give 0.

name: cxl_hdm_decode_init
prose: Precondition: cxlds, cxlhdm and info are valid, cxlhdm->regs.hdm_decoder is NULL or a mapped HDM decoder register block, cxlhdm->port is a registered CXL port, and info holds the DVSEC ranges. Behaviour: it reads the HDM global control register if the HDM block exists. If HDM decoding is already enabled, or the HDM block is absent and info->mem_enabled is set, it returns the result of devm_cxl_enable_mem(&port->dev, cxlds): that function sets the DVSEC memory-enable bit, returns 0 without registering a cleanup action if the bit was already set, and otherwise registers a devm action to clear it, returning the action registration's result or a config-space access error. If the HDM block is absent otherwise, it returns -ENODEV. If the block exists but is globally disabled and info->mem_enabled is clear, it calls devm_cxl_enable_hdm (setting the enable bit and registering a devm action to clear it; its error is returned) and then returns devm_cxl_enable_mem's result. If the block exists and info->mem_enabled is set, it walks from the port to the CXL root and returns -ENODEV (after an error message) if no root is found; then, for each DVSEC range, it looks for a child of the root that covers it with device_find_child and releases the found child with put_device, counting allowed ranges; it returns -ENXIO if none is allowed, and 0 otherwise.
note: checked pci.c:446-527, devm_cxl_enable_mem (289-299), cxl_set_mem_enable (261-282). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (no devm action when the memory-enable bit is already set); round 2 RIGHT (absent HDM block with DVSEC memory enabled goes to devm_cxl_enable_mem, not -ENODEV).

name: cxl_port_setup_targets
prose: Precondition: port holds a region reference for cxlr whose decoder is a switch decoder, cxled is an endpoint decoder whose memdev is an endpoint of port (cxl_rr_load and cxl_ep_load are assumed to return non-NULL). Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if cxl_rr->nr_targets is not a power of 2. If cxl_rr->nr_targets_set is nonzero it computes the peer distance up the port chain and checks whether ep->dport is already in cxlsd->target[0 .. nr_targets_set-1]: if so it returns the error of check_last_peer if nonzero, otherwise it leaves nr_targets_set unchanged and returns 0; if not, it skips the decoder setup and goes to the add-target step. If nr_targets_set is zero it computes the parent granularity and ways (from the region and root decoder when the parent is the root, otherwise from the parent port's decoder), the port's eiw and the new granularity, returning the error of granularity_to_eig, ways_to_eiw or eig_to_granularity if one fails, returns -ENXIO if iw exceeds 8 or cxlsd->nr_targets, and then: for an auto-assembled region (CXL_REGION_F_AUTO) it returns -ENXIO if the decoder's ways, granularity (when iw > 1), HPA range or enable flag do not match; otherwise it returns the error of check_interleave_cap if the setting is unsupported, and sets cxld->interleave_ways, interleave_granularity and hpa_range. At the add-target step it returns -ENXIO if nr_targets_set equals nr_targets; for an auto region it returns -ENXIO if cxlsd->target[nr_targets_set] is not ep->dport; otherwise it stores ep->dport and its port_id in cxlsd->target and cxld.target_map at index nr_targets_set. It then increments nr_targets_set (by 1 on the add-target path, by 0 on the already-present path) and returns 0. The decoder fields are written before the add-target check, but on that path nr_targets_set is 0 and nr_targets is at least 1, so the targets-full return cannot be taken after the fields were written; all other error returns happen before any write to the decoder fields or nr_targets_set.
note: slice cut head; function is cxl_port_setup_targets (region.c:1327-1533). Reviewer round 15 only half right: the fields are written at 1494-1498 before the full check at 1504, but that check is unreachable on that path (is_power_of_2 rejects nr_targets == 0, and nr_targets_set == 0 there). Rounds 1 and 2 RIGHT: already-present peer does not increment, and an unseen dport with nr_targets_set > 0 skips decoder field updates.

name: region_offset_to_dpa_result
prose: Precondition: cxlr is a committed CXL region with valid params, the caller holds both the region and dpa rwsems (lockdep-asserted), offset is an offset into the region's resource and result is writable. Behaviour: it derives eig and eiw from the region's interleave granularity and ways with granularity_to_eig and ways_to_eiw (return values ignored); if the root decoder has a spa_to_hpa callback it converts p->res->start + offset with it and takes hpa_offset relative to p->res->start, otherwise hpa_offset is offset. It computes the interleave position: for eiw < 8 the eiw bits starting at bit eig + 8 of hpa_offset, otherwise (hpa_offset >> (eig + 8)) modulo the number of ways. If the position is not below p->nr_targets it logs and returns -ENXIO. It then computes the DPA offset: bits [eig+7:0] of hpa_offset pass through; for eiw < 8 the remaining bits with bits [eig+eiw+7:0] cleared are shifted right by eiw (this also clears those bits in the local hpa_offset); for eiw >= 8 it is ((hpa_offset >> (eig + eiw)) / 3) << (eig + 8). Finally it searches p->targets for the endpoint decoder whose pos equals the position; if found it stores that decoder's memdev in result->cxlmd and cxl_dpa_resource_start(cxled) plus the DPA offset in result->dpa and returns 0; otherwise it logs an error and returns -ENXIO with result untouched.
note: slice cut head; real function is region_offset_to_dpa_result (region.c:3021-3107); no cxl_calc_dpa_offset_and_lookup exists. Old prose took hpa_offset and pos as parameters, which this function does not; the position is computed inside and an out-of-range position returns -ENXIO.

name: trans_stat_store
prose: Precondition: dev is a devfreq device, buf a NUL-terminated string, count its length. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if df->profile is NULL, and returns count without changing any state if df->max_state is 0 (this check comes before the parsing). Otherwise it parses buf with kstrtoint base 10 and returns -EINVAL if parsing fails or the value is not 0. It then takes df->lock, zeroes stats.time_in_state (max_state entries) and stats.trans_table (max_state * max_state entries), sets stats.total_trans to 0 and stats.last_update to get_jiffies_64(), releases the lock and returns count.
note: slice cut head; function is devfreq.c:1767-1795. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG for this tree: with max_state == 0 the function returns count at line 1777-1778 before total_trans and last_update are touched; old prose put the parse check ahead of the max_state check.

name: exynos_bus_ops_edev(enable_edev)
prose: Generated function exynos_bus_enable_edev(bus), expanded from exynos_bus_ops_edev(enable_edev). Precondition: bus is an initialised exynos_bus whose edev array has edev_count entries, each NULL or a devfreq-event device. Behaviour: it loops over the entries in index order, skips NULL ones, and calls devfreq_event_enable_edev on each other entry; if a call returns a negative value it returns that value immediately; the failing device has already been passed to the call, earlier devices stay as the calls left them, and later entries are not touched. It returns 0 if every call succeeded, including when edev_count is 0.
note: exynos-bus.c:44-59. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the failing device is the one whose call returned the error, so it was not left untouched.

name: at_xdmac_tx_status
prose: Precondition: chan is an at_xdmac channel; txstate may be NULL. Behaviour: it calls dma_cookie_status; if that returns DMA_COMPLETE, or txstate is NULL, it returns that status immediately (no lock and no runtime PM). Otherwise it calls pm_runtime_resume_and_get and returns DMA_ERROR without a residue if that fails. It takes atchan->lock and examines the first descriptor on atchan->xfers_list (not the one selected by the cookie, and the list is assumed non-empty). If that descriptor's transfer is not active it stores the full transfer size as the residue and unlocks. Otherwise, for peripheral-to-memory synchronised transfers it flushes the FIFO (busy-waiting for the flush status bit), then re-reads the next-descriptor, current microblock and INITD registers until they are consistent, up to AT_XDMAC_RESIDUE_MAX_RETRIES; if they never are, it sets the status to DMA_ERROR and unlocks without storing a residue. Otherwise it flushes again, subtracts the sizes of the microblocks already transferred, adds the current microblock's remaining size and stores the result with dma_set_residue. In every path after the runtime PM reference was taken, the lock is released with interrupts restored and the reference is dropped (mark_last_busy and put_autosuspend), and the function returns the status from dma_cookie_status (DMA_IN_PROGRESS) or DMA_ERROR.
note: slice cut head; the real function is at_xdmac_tx_status (at_xdmac.c:1540-1660); no at_xdmac_get_residue exists. Old prose said the cookie selects the descriptor and that DMA_SUCCESS is returned; neither matches the code (first list entry, status from dma_cookie_status).

name: at_xdmac_tasklet
prose: Precondition: the tasklet was scheduled for the channel, atchan->irq_status holds the pending channel status and the caller does not hold atchan->lock. Behaviour: if the channel is cyclic it returns the result of at_xdmac_handle_cyclic, which, under the lock, returns if xfers_list is empty and otherwise takes the head descriptor and, outside the lock, calls its callback only if its flags include DMA_PREP_INTERRUPT. For a non-cyclic channel it takes the lock; if neither AT_XDMAC_CIS_LIS nor any of RBEIS, WBEIS, ROIS is set in irq_status it unlocks and returns. If an error bit is set it calls at_xdmac_handle_error, which does nothing further if pm_runtime_resume_and_get fails (the channel is then not disabled by it), and otherwise logs the errors, disables the channel and waits until the status shows it disabled, and drops its runtime PM reference. It then takes the head descriptor of xfers_list; if it is not active it logs an error, unlocks and returns. Otherwise it completes the descriptor's cookie, removes it from the list, unlocks, invokes the callback only if DMA_PREP_INTERRUPT is set, runs dma_run_dependencies, retakes the lock, splices the descriptor's descs_list onto free_descs_list, calls at_xdmac_advance_work, unlocks and drops the runtime PM reference taken by at_xdmac_start_xfer.
note: checked at_xdmac.c:1702-1790. Matches the old prose on all listed points; added the handle_error pm failure case (reviewer round 2 RIGHT) and the list-empty cyclic case (original reviewer RIGHT).

name: jz4780_dma_tx_status
prose: Precondition: the caller does not hold jzchan->vchan.lock; if the cookie is not on the issued list, jzchan->desc must be non-NULL because it is dereferenced without a check. Behaviour: it takes vchan.lock with interrupts saved and calls dma_cookie_status, which sets the txstate fields (residue 0) when txstate is non-NULL and returns DMA_COMPLETE or DMA_IN_PROGRESS. If the status is DMA_COMPLETE or txstate is NULL it unlocks and returns that status. Otherwise it looks the cookie up on the issued list: if found, the residue is computed for that descriptor from its start; else if the cookie equals the active descriptor's cookie the residue is computed from the current hardware descriptor; else it is 0; the residue is stored with dma_set_residue. If the descriptor found on the issued list is also the active descriptor and the active descriptor's status has JZ_DMA_DCS_AR or JZ_DMA_DCS_HLT set the status becomes DMA_ERROR. The lock is released on every path and the status is returned.
note: checked dma-jz4780.c:641-674 and dma_cookie_status (dmaengine.h:68-83). Reviewer round 15 WRONG: dma_cookie_status returns only DMA_COMPLETE or DMA_IN_PROGRESS via dma_async_is_complete, so the NULL-txstate return is DMA_IN_PROGRESS; the first reviewer claim (no residue when txstate is NULL) is RIGHT.

name: axi_chan_is_hw_enable
prose: Precondition: chan is an initialised AXI DMA channel with valid chip, dw and hdata pointers. Behaviour: it reads DMAC_CHEN as a 64-bit value if hdata->nr_channels >= DMAC_CHAN_16 (16) and as a 32-bit value otherwise. For a channel id below 16 it returns whether bit id of the value is set. For id >= 16 it returns whether bit id + 16 (the channel's bit within the upper 32-bit word, DMAC_CHAN_BLOCK_SHIFT = 32 after BIT(id) >> 16) of the value is set. It has no other side effects.
note: slice cut head; function is axi_chan_is_hw_enable (dw-axi-dmac-platform.c:250-263). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: (BIT(id) >> 16) << 32 is bit id + 16.

name: idxd_drv_enable_wq
prose: Precondition: the caller holds wq->wq_lock (lockdep-asserted). Behaviour: it returns -ENXIO and sets idxd->cmd_status to IDXD_SCMD_DEV_NOT_ENABLED if the device is not IDXD_DEV_ENABLED; -EBUSY with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_ENABLED if the WQ is not disabled; -ENXIO with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_NO_GRP if the WQ has no group; -ENXIO with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_NO_NAME if its name is empty; -ENXIO with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_NO_SVM if it is shared but sharing is unsupported; and -ENXIO with IDXD_SCMD_WQ_NO_THRESH if it is shared with threshold 0. On a configurable device with PASID enabled it may set the WQ's PASID for kernel or shared WQs. It then calls idxd_device_config and idxd_wq_enable and, if either returns a negative value, returns it directly with cmd_status unchanged and without any disable call. It maps the portal with idxd_wq_map_portal (on a negative result sets IDXD_SCMD_WQ_PORTAL_ERR and calls idxd_wq_disable(wq, false), logging if that fails), sets client_count to 0, requests the irq with idxd_wq_request_irq (which does nothing and returns 0 unless the WQ type is kernel; on a negative result sets IDXD_SCMD_WQ_IRQ_ERR, unmaps the portal and disables the WQ, without calling idxd_wq_free_irq), allocates resources with idxd_wq_alloc_resources (on failure sets IDXD_SCMD_WQ_RES_ALLOC_ERR, frees the irq, unmaps the portal and disables) and initialises the percpu ref with idxd_wq_init_percpu_ref (on failure sets IDXD_SCMD_PERCPU_ERR, frees the resources, frees the irq, unmaps the portal and disables). It returns 0 when all steps succeed; the interrupt-related state is set only for kernel-type WQs.
note: checked device.c:1368-1495 and idxd_wq_request_irq (1326-1366). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (non-kernel WQs return 0 from idxd_wq_request_irq without requesting an irq); round 2 and the original claim RIGHT (no free_irq on request failure; cmd_status not set for config/enable failures).

name: perfmon_pmu_init
prose: Precondition: idxd is a valid idxd_device. Behaviour: it returns -ENODEV, allocating nothing, if idxd->perfmon_offset is 0, and -ENOMEM if the idxd_pmu allocation fails. It stores the allocation in idxd->idxd_pmu, names the PMU with sprintf as "dsa<id>" or "iax<id>" by device type (an unknown type goes to the free path with the initial -ENODEV), resets the perfmon registers, reads the capability register, and frees the idxd_pmu and clears idxd->idxd_pmu on the free path if the counter count, counter width, overflow interrupt/counter freeze, event category count or per-counter capability checks reject the hardware. It then records the capabilities, calls idxd_pmu_init and perf_pmu_register(..., -1), freeing the idxd_pmu and clearing idxd->idxd_pmu if registration fails, and returns the registration result (0 on success). The return value after the capability-check rejections is not -ENODEV: rc holds the result of the earlier sprintf (the length of the PMU name, a positive number), so those rejections return a positive value rather than a negative errno.
note: slice cut head; real function is perfmon_pmu_init (idxd/perfmon.c:474-562). Old prose said -ENODEV for unsupported capabilities, but rc is overwritten by sprintf's positive return value (lines 497-505) before the capability checks, so the `goto free` paths at 513-531 return that positive value.

name: sdma_config_channel
prose: Precondition: chan is a DMA channel embedded in a valid sdma_channel with its engine, register mapping and script_addrs set. Behaviour: it calls sdma_disable_channel, clears event_mask[0], event_mask[1], shp_addr and per_addr, and then calls sdma_config_ownership (ignoring its return value) with flags (event_override, mcu_override, dsp_override) of (false, true, true) for IMX_DMATYPE_DSP, (false, true, false) for IMX_DMATYPE_MEMORY and (true, true, false) for every other peripheral type; the function writes the three ownership override registers. It then calls sdma_get_pc and returns its nonzero result immediately, without the rest of the setup. For peripheral types other than MEMORY and DSP: if event_id1 is set it calls sdma_set_watermarklevel_for_p2p for ASRC and ASRC_SP and does nothing more for other types; if event_id1 is not set it calls sdma_set_watermarklevel_for_sais for MULTI_SAI and sets the event_id0 bit in event_mask; it then sets shp_addr to per_address and per_addr to per_address2. For MEMORY and DSP it sets watermark_level to 0. It returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is imx-sdma.c:1315-1366. Reviewer round 15 not applicable here: the ownership flags per type are in lines 1327-1337 (DSP, MEMORY, default); the claim about CCM/IPU/HDMI concerns sdma_get_pc, which was not re-read line by line. Old prose misdescribed the ownership calls (the flag names are event/mcu/dsp override, not directions).
